Jerry Zimmerer

Democratic candidate for 15th Court of Appeals, Chief Justice, Texas

Visiting judge, mediator and arbitrator; former Justice, Texas 14th Court of Appeals

Jerry (Gerald) Zimmerer is a Democrat and a former justice of Houston's 14th Court of Appeals, where he served from 2019 to 2024. He was unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary. He faces Republican Scott Brister, the court's appointed chief justice, in the first election for chief justice of the 15th Court of Appeals, which opened in 2024.

Where Zimmerer stands

Judicial independence
Says the 15th Court hears cases about what the Governor, Attorney General and state agencies may do, and should be decided by an experienced judge who owes nothing to the officials whose conduct is under review.
Court transparency and public access
Proposes acting as a 'Chief Educator' who uses technology to explain how the court decides cases. He would also give an annual State of the Judiciary address and hold community dialogue within the Code of Judicial Conduct.
Impartiality and conflicts of interest
Says he served on the 14th Court of Appeals as an impartial jurist who avoided conflicts of interest, and pledges to do the same as Chief Justice.
Elected vs. appointed judges
Points out that every seat on the 15th Court was filled by gubernatorial appointment, and calls November 3, 2026 the first time voters have a say in who sits on it.

Background

  • Justice, Texas 14th Court of Appeals (Houston), 2019–2024
  • Visiting judge, court-appointed mediator and arbitrator since leaving the bench
  • Founder, Advanced Dispute Resolutions, LLC
  • Former Director of International Arbitration, Texas Justice Center
  • Former Director of Education, Training and Credentialing, National Mediation & Conflict Solutions
  • Technology professional, AT&T Mobility (12 years), before returning to private practice
  • Practice areas: civil trial, health law, international arbitration
  • J.D., South Texas College of Law Houston
  • LL.M. in health law and LL.M. in international law, University of Houston
  • Unopposed winner of the 2026 Democratic primary for Chief Justice, 15th Court of Appeals
